blocks.name: 5' cap
blocks.note: m7G(5')ppp(5')N cap. A chemical modification at the 5' end, not a base, so it has no letters in the sequence. The cap is what tells the cell this is a real message worth translating rather than debris worth destroying.

blocks.name: 5' UTR (human alpha-globin)
blocks.note: Human alpha-globin 5' untranslated region. Real sequence, 37 nt, from ENST00000320868 (GRCh37). Sits between the cap and the start codon, and strongly affects how efficiently the message is translated.

blocks.name: Kozak

blocks.name: stop
blocks.note: Two stop codons in a row.

blocks.name: 3' UTR (human beta-globin)
blocks.note: Human beta-globin 3' untranslated region. Real sequence, 134 nt, from ENST00000335295 (GRCh37). Follows the stop codon and governs how long the message survives before being broken down. Contains the AATAAA polyadenylation signal at position 108, which marks where the poly-A tail is added.

blocks.name: poly-A tail
blocks.note: 100 adenines. Protects the message from being chewed up too quickly.

notes: Therapeutic mRNA typically replaces uridine with a modified base such as N1-methylpseudouridine, which greatly reduces the innate immune response to the RNA itself. That is a chemistry choice invisible in the letters below.
